_note: Artifact types, step 1. j2.py's flow does not read this file; tests/test files compare it with the Python it mirrors (prd/hld/lld/website) and the Artifacts tab reads it. kind type = a deliverable the department builds; kind record = evidence the run keeps. A file with * lists every match. Regexes are case-insensitive.

builder_tools._note: Claude's built-in tools, given to every builder in its own folder (a form may set its own tools and allow). builder: the guidance every builder with tools gets; atom_rules: what Adaptation's atom rules add for every form when builders have tools (missing capabilities); real_run: what they add for a form with a test runner (running a build for real, step 7); folder: the run's output folder for a form that names none. tools: the CLI tool list; allow: its permission rules; WebFetch(domain:*) also opens the sandbox's network to any host. Reads stay fenced to the folder by code (llm.cli_settings).

forms._note: How each form is built and checked, defined once. advisory_checks: check types whose failure is a warning on the result, never a gate (a website's browser checks, a document's section checks). A type names its form; every field it leaves out comes from here ({name}, {label}, {noun} and {sections} are filled from the type; {practice} is the form's practice_rule for a type whose recommended_practice is true, else empty). output: what a form makes, "file" (one file) or "folder" (a folder of files its builder writes with the tools the form declares: tools is the CLI tool list, allow its permission rules, test_runner the command a test is run with, {target} the test file; J2_AGENT_TOOLS=1 only). browser_checks: the check types code runs in headless Chrome (the plan format lists the others; the atom rules describe these). cost.item_parts: the kinds of done-when item (part: the rate-card part it costs at least; about: what Identity reads to tag each item at J2.a; default: the kind of an untagged item; mock_words: the mock Identity's tagging only). expect_kinds: an expected-output kind -> the check type that verifies it.

page.about: a web page: one HTML entry file, with any style, script or image files beside it, checked in a browser

document.about: a written document in markdown, by sections, from a section template
document.practice_rule: ; a line labelled "Recommended practice:" may give general good practice the brief does not state and is not an invented fact, but every number, name, price, date, law and claim about the business in it must still come from the charter or the Requester's answers

rubric.text: Every section does the job its name says, for the charter's audience
Specific and checkable: names, numbers and rules are stated, not implied
No invented facts: every fact comes from the brief or the Requester's answers, or is labelled "Assumption:"; the evidence quotes each unlabelled claim not in the brief{practice}

document.done: Done: the {label} is workable. Every done-when item, rubric item and necessary condition passes.

item_parts.about: an item about the requirements, the components, or the pages and sections
any other section of the document

agent.about: a folder of files a builder writes and runs with its tools (code, scripts, configs), with a test it runs

rubric.text: The {lower} does the one job the charter names, and nothing else
It touches only what the charter says it may touch
Every must-never-do item in the charter is enforced in the {lower}'s own instructions or code
Its test exercises the main job, and it passed when the builder ran it in the sandbox

agent.done: Done: the {label} is workable. Its test passed in the sandbox and every done-when item, rubric item and necessary condition passes.

types.name: prd
types.label: Product requirements

rubric.text: Every requirement is specific and testable
Goals and success metrics are measurable
Users and problem are consistent with the requirements
Out of scope is explicit
No invented facts: every fact comes from the brief or the Requester's answers, or is labelled "Assumption:"; the evidence quotes each unlabelled claim not in the brief{practice}

types.done: Done: the PRD is workable. Every done-when item, rubric item and necessary condition passes.

types.name: hld
types.label: High-level design

rubric.text: Every component has one clear responsibility
The data flow names every form and integration the pages need
Hosting, deployment and risks are explicit
Consistent with the PRD: every requirement has a component
No invented facts: every fact comes from the brief or the Requester's answers or the PRD, or is labelled "Assumption:"; the evidence quotes each unlabelled claim not in them

types.done: Done: the HLD is workable. Every done-when item, rubric item and necessary condition passes.

types.name: lld
types.label: Low-level design

rubric.text: Every page section has an id and implements at least one component
Every interactive element has a selector, a trigger and a behaviour
Every form field has a type, a required flag and a validation rule
Consistent with the HLD: every component is built by a section
No invented facts: every fact comes from the brief or the Requester's answers or the earlier documents, or is labelled "Assumption:"; the evidence quotes each unlabelled claim

types.done: Done: the LLD is workable. Every done-when item, rubric item and necessary condition passes.

types.name: website
types.label: Website

rubric.text: Consistent styling: the whole page follows the style guide (same fonts, colours, button and card styles)
Readable contrast: text is easy to read against its background (WCAG AA)
Clear hierarchy: one main heading, headings in order, the most important things stand out
One obvious main action: a visitor can tell at once what to do next
Easy navigation: a visitor can reach every section quickly, on a phone too
Tap targets are big enough on phones (at least 44x44px; 24x24px for the cells or keys of a dense grid or keypad)
Images have alt text

types.done: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.

item_parts.about: a form visitors fill in and send (an order, a booking, an enquiry, a sign-up)
something visitors operate on the page (a filter, search, slider, calculator, tabs, an animation)
how the page looks or fits a screen (layout on phones, colours, fonts, no horizontal scroll)
any other content section of the page
